memory_update.text: LEU should remain the primary underfollowed public candidate for the nuclear fuel-cycle node because it has direct HALEU/enrichment exposure and is much narrower than utilities, reactor developers, or diversified industrials.
CCJ is the reference public leader for uranium and fuel-services/conversion economics, useful as a benchmark even if less underfollowed.
BWXT is a public advanced-fuel and nuclear-fabrication candidate, but later layers must separate commercial advanced-reactor upside from defense/government baseline revenue.
US uranium conversion appears strategically important but may not have a clean public pure-play; Honeywell/ConverDyn is a key asset mapping but likely too diluted for clean equity exposure.
Conversion may be the tightest commercial bottleneck, but clean public exposure appears limited; Honeywell/ConverDyn is relevant for mapping, not a pure-play candidate.
Centrus Energy should remain the primary public reference candidate for domestic enrichment and HALEU in this node.
BWX Technologies should remain on the map for advanced fuel fabrication/TRISO, but later layers must test materiality versus defense and nuclear-services revenue.
Energy Fuels is an underfollowed second-order upstream candidate: domestic uranium feedstock exposure is real, but it is not the same bottleneck as conversion, enrichment, or HALEU.
LEU should remain the primary public-market reference candidate for HALEU/enrichment within the nuclear fuel-cycle node.
BWXT is the strongest public advanced-fuel fabrication reference, but its size and diversified nuclear/defense exposure reduce underfollowed purity.
UUUU is a plausible underfollowed second-order domestic uranium and milling candidate, but it is upstream of the most acute HALEU/conversion bottleneck.
ASPI belongs in speculative shadow tracking only until licensing, production, and binding customer evidence improves.

Uranium conversion may be a critical chokepoint, but the clean public pure-play appears missing; Honeywell/ConverDyn should be tracked as a non-pure mega-cap context anchor rather than a main discovery-lane candidate.

SOLS is a newly public, underappreciated uranium conversion mapping: formerly hidden inside Honeywell, now a Nasdaq-listed specialty-materials company with the only US UF6 conversion facility at Metropolis Works.
ASPI belongs in the speculative shadow lane for HALEU/enrichment because its exposure depends on technology validation, regulatory approvals, QLE economics, and binding offtake.
LTBR is not a near-term conversion/enrichment bottleneck supplier but may be useful to track as an advanced fuel-design option if reactor customers and regulators validate its technology.

BWXT should be handled in a later pass or as a reference name for advanced fuel fabrication/TRISO; it is relevant but larger, better-covered, and less aligned with this pass's underfollowed small/mid-cap focus.

The investable bottleneck map for nuclear fuel cycle appears uneven: enrichment has LEU and speculative ASPI, conversion now has SOLS, advanced fuel fabrication has fewer clean public names, and private entities such as X-energy/General Matter remain important non-public chokepoints.

node: Nuclear fuel cycle: uranium, conversion, enrichment, HALEU, fabrication
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expansion found that the cleanest US-listed direct exposure remains sparse. Centrus is the most direct public HALEU/enrichment chokepoint candidate. Cameco is the large public uranium plus conversion/fuel-services reference leader. BWX Technologies is the public advanced nuclear fuel/fabrication and nuclear-components leader, but it is already well followed and less small-cap. Honeywell is included only as a context/reference name because its Metropolis/ConverDyn exposure appears strategically critical but financially diluted inside a mega-cap. The key coverage gap is that conversion may be one of the tightest bottlenecks, yet the investable pure-play public expression is weak or absent. Layer 1B expansion for the nuclear fuel-cycle node finds that investable exposure is unusually sparse beyond uranium miners. The strongest chokepoint signals are conversion, enrichment/HALEU, and advanced fuel fabrication. Centrus is the clearest public enrichment/HALEU name; Honeywell is the buried U.S. conversion exposure through Metropolis Works/ConverDyn but is too diversified to be a clean expression; BWX Technologies is a public advanced fuel/TRISO fabrication exposure but is already relatively visible and larger-cap; Energy Fuels is a smaller U.S.-listed upstream uranium supplier that may provide second-order domestic fuel-cycle exposure, though it is less directly tied to conversion/enrichment bottlenecks. Expanded the investable universe around the nuclear fuel-cycle chokepoint with emphasis on smaller or more direct public exposure. The cleanest public chokepoint exposure
